title: Vice President: Align Directors Around a Shared Outcome
prompt: Two directors have conflicting targets. Acquisition is rewarded for new accounts; Service is rewarded for low cost per case. Acquisition launched a campaign that increased complex new accounts by 30%; Service limited onboarding support to meet its cost target. Complaints rose, but no shared customer-completion measure exists. Lead a discussion with both directors, represented by one AI using labeled perspectives.

rubric.label: Identify the incentive conflict
rubric.description: Distinguishes local success from organization-wide outcomes.

anchors.0: Blames one director without examining target definitions.
anchors.4: Traces incomplete onboarding and hidden repeat contacts across both measures, avoids unsupported personal blame and identifies the missing end-to-end outcome.

rubric.label: Set shared accountability
rubric.description: Creates a joint outcome without erasing distinct responsibilities.

anchors.0: Adds a vague teamwork target or makes both directors own everything.
anchors.2: Proposes a shared completion measure and joint review.
anchors.4: Agrees a shared customer outcome with quality/cost guardrails, retains named owners for acquisition and service decisions, and secures authority to change the old incentives.

anchors.0: Adds work with no capacity or declares success from fewer complaints alone.
anchors.2: Runs a pilot and reviews results.
anchors.4: Funds a bounded four-week pilot by reprioritizing work, examines comparable cohorts and repeat contacts, and defines adjustment/stop criteria and how learning will change targets.

reference.scenario: Two directors have conflicting targets. Acquisition is rewarded for new accounts; Service is rewarded for low cost per case. Acquisition launched a campaign that increased complex new accounts by 30%; Service limited onboarding support to meet its cost target. Complaints rose, but no shared customer-completion measure exists. Lead a discussion with both directors, represented by one AI using labeled perspectives.

facts.value: Acquisition’s reported growth includes accounts that never completed onboarding. Service’s cost measure excludes repeat contacts handled by another team. Neither director designed these definitions alone.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about metric definitions or attribution

facts.value: The executive team can amend the targets. Both directors can assign people to a four-week shared pilot if priorities are explicitly reduced elsewhere.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about authority or pilot capacity

model_points: Traces incomplete onboarding and hidden repeat contacts across both measures, avoids unsupported personal blame and identifies the missing end-to-end outcome.
Agrees a shared customer outcome with quality/cost guardrails, retains named owners for acquisition and service decisions, and secures authority to change the old incentives.
Funds a bounded four-week pilot by reprioritizing work, examines comparable cohorts and repeat contacts, and defines adjustment/stop criteria and how learning will change targets.

probes.trigger: candidate keeps both original targets unchanged
probes.question: What behavior will each director still be rewarded for?
What harm could that metric conceal?
How will a frontline team know who decides an exception?

fair_alternatives: A balanced set of shared and local measures is valid; one metric need not carry all accountability.
Immediate target suspension can be valid if the executive authority and temporary decision rule are explicit.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Repair an incentive system
learning_drills.prompt: Write one shared outcome, two balancing measures and a decision-rights map for the pilot. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
